title: OpenScout Montage Score (45s)
purpose: Original instrumental soundtrack for the OpenScout 45-second product montage

generator.path: Preframe configured music slot (lib/provider.ts readMusicModelConfig + getMiniMaxApiKey); credential resolved from environment, never printed
generator.prompt: A 45-second modern kinetic ambient electronic instrumental for a software product montage. Warm controlled low end: a round soft sub and gentle analog bass pulse that never booms. Crisp restrained percussion: light tactile clicks, brushed hats and soft rim ticks, precise and understated, no big drums. Motifs of signal, routing and connection: short pinging tones that hand off between left and right, quiet telemetry blips, granular air, subtle delay trails suggesting spatial movement across a wide stereo field. Premium and slightly mysterious mood, minor-leaning harmony, clean sustained pads and a few clear bell-like tones. Natural quiet intro over the first 8 seconds, patient build with added pulse and widening texture through the middle, a small lift near 30 seconds, then subtract and resolve into a warm settled ending with a clean natural tail. No vocals, no spoken words, no lyrics, no choir, no cheesy corporate uplift, no supersaw anthem, no lo-fi hip hop beat, no trailer risers, no impacts, no drops, no dense melody.

edit.rationale: The 199s generation contains a natural quiet intro and build at its head and the composition's own resolved outro at its tail. Both were used so the 45s cut has a real intro, build and composed resolution instead of an arbitrary trim.
processing: 3.100 s equal-power (qsin) crossfade joining the two segments in a low-energy passage
transparent peak limiter, ceiling -2.5 dBFS sample (attack 5 ms, release 60 ms) — engages only on isolated transients
0.650 s fade-out from 44.350 s to a silent tail
encode stereo 24-bit PCM WAV at 48 kHz, then MP3 320 kbps CBR and AAC 256 kbps

master.headroomNote: Conservative bed level with ~1.6 dB true-peak headroom; raise or duck at the edit rather than re-limiting.
